why: The student reads `if (x > 0);` as if it still controls the next println, so they say positive is not printed. In Java the lone `;` is the whole body of the if, so the println always runs and positive is printed.

concepts.quote: positive is not printed, because x > 0 is false.
concepts.why: They read the semicolon as just ending a clause, not as an empty statement that forms the whole body of the if.

concepts.quote: positive is not printed, because x > 0 is false.
concepts.why: They take the println as the if's body, which goes against the rule if (<boolean expression>) <statement>, where the statement here is `;`.
